newsitem.title: CHINA: China foreign investment seen down in 1997.
newsitem.headline: China foreign investment seen down in 1997.

text.p: Foreign investment in China is forecast to shrink in 1997 to $30-40 billion, the official Xinhua news agency said on Monday.

"Although the figure is smaller than that for 1996, it is still large for China's economic development," Xinhua quoted Li Xiaoxi, a researcher with the State Council, or cabinet, as saying. It gave no reason for the decline.
Overseas investment in China was about $48 billion last year, official figures show.
China would continue to attract foreign funds with a series of more flexible macro-economic control measures following Beijing's success in reining in inflation, Li said.
Reform of state enterprises would provide foreign investors with more opportunities, he said without elaborating.

The return to Chinese rule of the British colony of Hong Kong on July 1 this year and global economic development would also help stimulate foreign investment in the mainland, Li said. He gave no further details.
"The government is optimistic about foreign investment for this year," Xinhua quoted Ma Xiuhong, director of the Ministry of Foreign Trade's foreign investment department, as saying.
Foreign investment in China was $4.66 billion in the first two months of 1997, a rise of 1.5 percent from the year-ago period, official figures show.
